chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man divorces a pregnant woman, he provides for her until she gives birth to her child. And if she nurses him, he gives her her wage, and he does not harm her, unless he finds someone who is cheaper in wage than her. If she accepts that wage, then she is more entitled to her son until she weans him."

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And if the wife is a slave woman, her waiting period is three menstrual periods. And if her menstruation has ceased due to a chance occurrence (old age), her waiting period is forty-five days. (466) 65 Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated that from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a free man who has a slave wife, or a slave man who has a free wife, what is her divorce count and what is her waiting period? He said: 'The Sunnah for women in divorce is that if she is free, her divorce is three, and her waiting period is three menstrual periods. And if a free man has a slave wife, her divorce is two divorces, and her waiting period is one menstrual period.'

key_terms.تَضَعُ حَمْلَهَا: She gives birth to her child

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for divorce, maintenance, and waiting period for pregnant or nursing women in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the financial obligations of a husband towards a divorced pregnant wife, emphasizing that maintenance continues until childbirth and nursing is compensated unless a more economical option is available, thereby protecting the mother's economic stability. It further clarifies the distinct legal rulings for slave women, noting their shorter waiting period (*iddah*) of three menstrual cycles or forty-five days if post-menopausal, a ruling derived from the Prophet's tradition as reported by Abu Ja'far. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between free and slave women in matters of divorce and custody, rooted in the practical application of Quranic verses on divorce.
